questions.question: Which of the following is a common adaptation that helps prey animals avoid being caught by predators?
options: Having large, sharp tearing teeth
Developing bright colors to attract attention
Being nocturnal to stay hidden in the dark
Having a highly developed ability to run fast in open fields

questions.question: Which physical adaptation is most characteristic of a predator trying to locate and catch prey?
options: Excellent eyesight for spotting targets from a distance
Dull-colored fur for hiding from larger herbivores
Edible seeds that can be easily dispersed
The ability to produce toxic chemicals to deter insects

questions.question: What does it mean when a toxic substance in an ecosystem is described as "persistent"?
options: It quickly dissolves in water and becomes harmless.
It remains in the environment for a long time without breaking down.
It is rapidly excreted by any organism that consumes it.
It only affects the lowest level of the food chain.

questions.question: Which group of organisms in a food chain is typically most severely damaged by the bioaccumulation of toxic substances?
options: Primary producers
Decomposers
Top predators
Herbivores

questions.question: A habitat contains both biotic and abiotic components. Which of the following represents an abiotic part of a habitat?
options: Microorganisms in the soil
Non-living physical factors like water and temperature
Small insects living under rocks
Decaying leaves on the forest floor

questions.question: In an ecosystem, which organisms are classified as producers because they can make their own food?
options: Fungi that decompose leaf litter
Herbivorous insects that eat leaves
Plants and some specialized microorganisms
Carnivorous animals that hunt prey

questions.question: Why are humans and other animals classified as consumers in a food chain?
options: They synthesize their own food using sunlight.
They get their food by consuming other organisms.
They release energy directly into the soil for plants.
They break down rocks to absorb minerals.

questions.question: What do the arrows in a food chain diagram specifically represent?
options: The direction of movement of the animals
The transfers of biomass from one organism to another
The release of oxygen into the atmosphere
The path of water through the ecosystem

questions.question: What is represented by a food web diagram?
options: The total number of individual organisms in a single habitat
Several interconnected food chains within a community
The stages of decomposition of a single dead organism
The movement of water through different living things

questions.question: What process must occur for plants to produce edible seeds and fruits, involving the transfer of pollen from the anthers to the stigma?
options: Photosynthesis
Transpiration
Pollination
Germination

questions.question: How do plants and animals demonstrate interdependence regarding reproduction and spreading offspring?
options: Plants provide animals with shelter in exchange for water.
Plants rely on insects for pollination and birds for seed dispersal.
Animals depend on plants to purify all the drinking water.
Plants rely on birds to build nests that protect plant roots.

questions.question: Why are pollinators crucial for human food security?
options: They directly produce meat and dairy products for humans.
They ensure there is enough food to feed the human population by helping crops reproduce.
They filter harmful chemicals out of the agricultural soil.
They eat agricultural pests that would otherwise destroy crops.

questions.question: What is meant by the term "biodiversity" in an ecosystem?
options: The total mass of all living organisms in an area
The number of different species that live in a place
The speed at which energy is transferred up a food chain
The rate of reproduction among a single species of plant

questions.question: How can the genetic diversity of plants be conserved for the future?
options: By only growing a single crop species worldwide
By using large amounts of chemical fertilizers
Through the use of seed banks and other gene banks
By removing all insects from agricultural fields

questions.question: How do certain pesticides help crops grow by targeting other plants, such as weeds?
options: They directly fertilize the soil surrounding the crops.
They kill competing plants so crops have better access to resources.
They accelerate the pollination process of the crop plants.
They increase the genetic diversity of the crops.

questions.question: In what ways do humans have a negative impact on biodiversity?
options: By establishing nature reserves and seed banks
By practicing crop rotation and organic farming
Through habitat destruction and environmental pollution
By encouraging the growth of native plant species
